# From Delegation to Capability {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Save the good prompt once. Run it forever.

## The Problem with a Great Prompt {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="why" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.15em;"}
That perfect RICE delegation from Day 1 is gone the moment the chat closes. You retype it
every week.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
A **Skill** turns it into a button you press by name.
:::

# What a Skill Is {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

A library of books you open when needed

## Anatomy of a Skill {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="anatomy" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
Your Skills are a **library**. Each Skill is a **book** — a written playbook for one
recurring task.
:::

. . .

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5em; font-size: 0.95em;"}
Cowork keeps the whole shelf, but **only opens the book your task calls for** — not every
book, every time. *(just like the office puts only the relevant page on the desk)*
:::

. . .

::: {.incremental}
- **The title on the spine** — the trigger that tells Cowork which book to pull
- **What's written inside** — the steps, in plain language
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## Portable idea
Other apps call this a **GPT**, a **Gem**, or a **saved prompt**. Same idea: a reusable
playbook.
:::

# Demo — "Meeting Recap" {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

Your Day-1 delegation, now a Skill

## Save the Delegation as a Skill {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="recap" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.8em;"}
**Name:** Meeting Recap &nbsp;•&nbsp; **Trigger:** *"recap these notes"*

**Steps:** 1) extract Summary · 2) list Decisions · 3) pull Action Items with Owner +
**Deadline** · 4) flag anything with no owner under Open Questions · 5) keep it under 200 words
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
That's the RICE prompt from Day 1 — written down once, as a book on the shelf.
:::

## Invoke It on Fresh Input {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="recap" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7; font-size: 0.85em;"}
Skill saved — now just **type the trigger** on any new notes:
:::

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; font-style: italic; font-size: 0.85em; text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
"**Recap these notes**: budget review — approved the new hire, deferred the office move,

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #00C9A7; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}

# When the Job Is *Calculation* {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

A Skill follows steps — a **script** does the math

## Skill vs. Script {auto-animate=true}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
**Skill**

Instructions the agent **reads and follows** — a written playbook, in plain language.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
**Script**

Code the agent **writes and runs** to compute — exact, the same way every single row.
:::
:::
:::
::::

. . .

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
The brain in a jar **estimates** — and can slip on arithmetic. A computer **computes the
same way every time.** So for exact math, the agent doesn't do it in its head — it writes a script.
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## You still never touch code
This is Day 1's *"saved, repeatable steps"* — now done as real code. **You never write or
even see it:** describe what you want, the agent **writes and runs the script**, you get the result.
:::

## Demo — "Expense Crunch" {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="calc" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
You have a spreadsheet of raw expenses. You want totals by category, the outliers flagged,
and a clean summary — every month.
:::

. . .

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; font-style: italic; font-size: 0.85em; text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
"From `expenses_export.csv`, total spend by category, flag any line over 5,000 SAR, and save
a summary sheet."
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Sample data: [`expenses_export.csv`](../data/expenses_export.csv) — or rank vendors from
[`vendor_quotes.csv`](../data/vendor_quotes.csv).
:::

## Why a Script Here {auto-animate=true}

::: {.incremental}
- **Exact, every row** — the script computes, it doesn't estimate
- **Reproducible next month** — same script, same method; no formula errors, no copy-paste
- **You get the result, not the code** — describe it once, the agent writes and runs it
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## Pair it with "double-check"
For anything with money in it, ask it to compute **twice and compare** before you trust the numbers.
:::

# A Starter Library {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

Your shelf grows one book at a time

## Skills Employees Actually Use {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
| You say… | The Skill it pulls |
|---|---|
| "recap these notes" | **Meeting Recap** → summary + action items |
| "roll up the team updates" | **Status Roll-Up** → one weekly summary |
| "summarize this document" | **Doc Briefer** → 1-page summary + key points |
| "draft a reply to this" | **Inbox Drafter** → on-tone email draft |
| "compare these quotes" | **Quote Comparer** → ranked table + recommendation |
| "crunch these expenses" | **Expense Cruncher** → totals + outliers *(writes a script)* |
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #00C9A7; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
Your library grows **one book at a time.**
:::

# Build: Package One Skill {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

From your backlog

## Hands-On {auto-animate=true}

::: {.callout-tip}
## Steps
1. Pick a recurring task from your backlog.
2. Save its delegation as a **Skill** (name + trigger + steps).
3. **Run it twice** on different inputs to prove it generalizes.
4. Log the recurring weekly saving in your **Time Log**.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
Built once. Reused forever. That's the productivity flywheel.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-style: italic; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
**Refine:** swap Skills with a neighbor — *I like / I wish / I wonder.*
:::

:::

:::

## Key Takeaways {.sdaia-dark background-color="#1C355E"}

::: {.incremental}
1. **A Skill = a saved playbook** — your RICE delegation, written down once
2. **Anatomy** — a name, a trigger, and the steps; a book the agent opens on command
3. **It generalizes** — same Skill, any new input
4. **Skill vs. Script** — instructions the agent *follows* vs. code it *writes & runs* to compute exactly
5. **Build a library** — one book at a time, from your backlog; plain chat for one-offs
:::
